# Native transport fixtures

Retain all ABI1–4 samples as compatibility/refusal references. The ABI5 toy snapshot, UTC label and toy sky samples advance only the first version word of their ABI4 equivalents; existing behavioral coverage remains intact.

The new `slice-geometry-v5`, `slice-snapshot-v5` and `slice-sky-v5` samples use seed71449, configured UTC2026-06-22T11:22:30Z, camera target ENU(0,0,0) with500m interest, then20 explicit ticks at1×. Geometry is the full58-row extract. The snapshot contains all30 identities, including actual fine positions and four exact summaries. Both snapshot and sky deliberately store hash0 as a transport sentinel; live hash semantics are checked separately. The matching captured instant is11:22:32Z.

Source identities/topology/counts/time/version words are exact. Static/dynamic positions/normals are Tier3: tests compare their numeric values/invariants with explicit metre/normal tolerances, rather than promoting every coordinate byte into a Tier1 golden. Dedicated calendar/sun output retains ADR0030's bit guarantee. Rust's source-topology golden separately pins integer ear selection; source coverage, winding and normals are checked independently.

The new samples were generated on arm64 macOS from the built library with `python3 core/crates/ws-ffi/tests/generate-slice-fixtures.py /absolute/path/to/libws_ffi.dylib` (use the matching `.so` on Linux). This is an explicit maintenance command, never a test/CI regeneration step. Any accepted version's later golden change follows the testing policy.

## ABI6 current inspection samples

The six existing-layout `*-v6.hex` samples preserve every v5 byte after the ABI word; v1–5 files remain unchanged. New `inspect-resident-v6.hex` (1099bytes) and `inspect-building-v6.hex` (299bytes) are generated by the explicit generator at seed71449, UTC2026-06-22T11:22:30Z, camera target0/radius500 and20physical steps. Their canonical-hash field is explicitly zero as a transport sentinel, like prior slice samples; it is not a cross-platform world-hash golden. New integer identity/need/schedule/event fields pin wire interpretation. The generator writes new v6 names only.


ADR0033 adds v7 samples without replacing v1–6 files. Six existing-layout v7 bodies are byte-identical to v6 beyond the ABI word (hash sentinels remain documented zeros). New inspection schema2 has identity schema2, resident sex at136 and health/life at state-relative56/60; resident output is1103bytes, building299bytes for the shared cohort. Actual native generation remains the fixture source, compared with pure core fields and the independent vitals golden.

ADR0034 adds ABI8 samples while preserving all ABI1–7 files. Existing-layout bodies differ only in the ABI word. Inspection schema3 appends32 resident-state bytes; healthy resident sample1135bytes, building299bytes. `inspect-ill-v8` and `consequences-v8` are generated from one actual severity5/two-tick command after the existing sample boundary; their hash fields use the same explicit zero sentinel. Consequence rows preserve actual producer IDs and direct cause classes. Generation is explicit, never performed by tests/CI.

ADR0038 adds ABI9 samples while preserving all ABI1–8 files. Every existing-layout v9 body, slice and toy, is byte-identical to v8 beyond the ABI word. `consequences-bless-v9` (bless curing the sample illness: rows14,12), `consequences-storm-v9` (a one-minute storm run past its end: rows16,18,19, subject0) and `consequences-gathering-v9` (a gathering call at the first summary building: root row20 only) are generated after the existing sequence; the generator reads each root with `ws_slice_last_root`, since a storm root has no actor to inspect. Generation is explicit, never performed by tests/CI.

ADR0039 adds ABI10 samples while preserving all ABI1–9 files. Every v10 body is byte-identical to v9 beyond the ABI word, as the generator and a hand-advanced toy snapshot, UTC label and toy sky confirm. `ws_slice_god` has no fixture; the Rust and C smoke tests pin its layout directly. Generation is explicit, never performed by tests/CI.
